CPU、内存、磁盘各自在忙什么: What CPUs, memory and drives do
打开应用、输入文字、点击保存，看似连续的动作，其实由不同硬件接力完成。本章用一次: Opening an app, typing and saving feel continuous, but different hardware handles each step. Follow a note-editing session to connect instruction execution with registers, cache, memory and storage.
用取指、译码、执行解释程序如何运行，区分时钟周期与指令周期。: Explain execution through fetch, decode and execute, distinguishing clock cycles from instruction cycles.
按寄存器、缓存、内存、磁盘说明容量、速度与持久性的取舍。: Compare capacity, speed and persistence across registers, cache, RAM and drives.
解释再次打开应用可能更快、未保存文字可能丢失的原因。: Explain why reopening an app may be faster and why unsaved text may be lost.
会打开应用、编辑文字和保存文件即可，不要求编程基础。: Know how to open an app, edit text and save files; no programming experience required.
知道程序和文件都需要存放空间；本章会解释运行空间与长期存储的区别。: Know that programs and files need storage. This chapter separates working memory from long-term storage.
从打开笔记应用到保存一句话: From opening a notes app to saving a sentence
你双击本地笔记应用。操作系统建立进程，把运行所需的代码和数据按需装入内存，并非一: You double-click a local notes app. The OS creates a process and loads required code and data into memory as needed, not necessarily the whole app at once. If file contents are already in the OS's memory cache, reopening may need fewer drive reads.
轮到应用获得 CPU 时间后，处理器取得机器指令、译码并执行。计算常使用寄存器中: Once the app gets CPU time, the processor fetches, decodes and executes machine instructions. Computation often uses register operands; memory access typically passes through caches. Displaying a window involves many instructions and system services, not one “open app” instruction.
你输入“今天学计算机”。应用更新内存中的文本，CPU 反复访问代码和附近数据时可: You type “Learning computers today.” The app updates text in memory. Repeated access to code and nearby data may hit CPU cache. Hardware manages that cache; it is not where you manually save files. The OS file cache is a different kind of cache.
点击保存后，应用请求系统写文件，数据可能先停在内存中的写缓冲，再落到 SSD 或: Saving asks the OS to write a file. Data may first remain in memory buffers before reaching an SSD or hard drive. Reliable persistence also involves flushing and device guarantees. Unsaved changes without a recovery copy usually cannot be recovered after power loss.
同一串 0 和 1 不会自己说明含义：它可以表示整数，也可以是文字编码的一部分。: A string of zeros and ones does not explain itself: it might be an integer or part of encoded text. Start with a byte, calculate place values, compare unsigned and two's-complement interpretations, then explore text encoding. The binary lab covers integers, not text encoding.
根据位权把一个八位无符号二进制数转换成十进制。: Convert an eight-bit unsigned binary number to decimal using place values.
区分同一八位位串的无符号与二补码解释，说明零和负数的边界。: Compare unsigned and two's-complement interpretations, including zero and negative limits.
区分字符、Unicode 码点与编码字节，解释 UTF-8 的变长特性。: Distinguish characters, Unicode code points and encoded bytes; explain variable-length UTF-8.
知道计算机用内存保存运行中的数据，文件可以存放文字。: Know that memory holds working data and files can contain text.
会做整数加法，知道乘以二会翻倍；不要求编程或进制基础。: Be comfortable with integer addition and doubling; no programming or number-base experience required.
同一串位如何表示数值和文字: How the same bits represent numbers and text
先数位：八个开关组成一个字节: Count the bits: eight switches make a byte
把内存中的一个字节想成八个只取 0 或 1 的开关。八位共有 256 种组合，0: Think of a byte as eight switches, each either 0 or 1. Eight bits give 256 combinations; 01000001 is one of them. The pattern alone does not specify a number or text. Distinguish bits from bytes: eight bits are not eight bytes.
算位权：从位串读出整数: Use place values to read an integer
先约定按无符号整数解释 01000001。从右向左的位权是 1、2、4、8、16: Interpret 01000001 as unsigned. From right to left, the weights are 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64 and 128. Add the weights of the 1 bits to get 65. Toggle switches in the lab to see bits and values change together. Eight unsigned bits range from 0 to 255.
把最高位打开得到 11000001：无符号读作 193，固定八位二补码则读作 -: Turning on the top bit gives 11000001: unsigned 193, but eight-bit two's complement -63 because the top weight is -128. A top bit of 0 means nonnegative, including zero; all ones means -1. The lab shows both results. The interpretation changes, not the stored bits.
读文字：编码连接码点与字节: Read text: encoding connects code points and bytes
回到 01000001，按 ASCII 或 UTF-8 解码就是字母 A；但不是: 01000001 decodes as A in ASCII or UTF-8, but not every character fits in one byte. Unicode assigns code points; UTF-8 encodes them in one to four bytes. The character “中” uses three; some extension ideographs use four. Explore this in the encoding card; the binary lab does not encode text.
人写的代码怎么变成机器指令: How source code becomes executable instructions
打开网页时，域名解析、传输协议、封装与逐跳转发各有分工。本章沿着一次请求认识四层: Loading a page involves name resolution, transport, encapsulation and hop-by-hop forwarding. Follow a request through four layers, then compare TCP and UDP using a live call. The diagram simplifies HTTP/1.1 over TCP, IP and Ethernet, omitting TLS and segmentation. It is not to byte scale, and not all HTTP uses TCP.
区分应用层、传输层、网络层、链路层的职责，读懂封装与解封装。: Distinguish the application, transport, internet and link layers; understand encapsulation and decapsulation.
按可靠性、有序性和时效需求比较 TCP 与 UDP，不把 UDP 等同于更快。: Compare TCP and UDP by reliability, ordering and deadlines, without assuming UDP is faster.
说明 DNS、HTTP 与 IP 转发如何配合，以及各自不能保证什么。: Explain how DNS, HTTP and IP forwarding cooperate and what each does not guarantee.
知道浏览器访问网站时，需要与另一台计算机上的服务交换数据。: Know that visiting a website exchanges data with a service on another computer.
知道数据可以表示为字节；不要求掌握报文格式、子网计算或网络编程。: Know that data can be represented as bytes. No packet formats, subnet calculations or network programming required.
打开一个网页，数据怎样抵达对端: How a webpage request reaches its destination
解析地址：先找到服务在哪: Resolve the address: find the service
你输入网站域名，浏览器需要可用的服务器地址。地址可能来自缓存；没有可用结果时，再: After you enter a domain, the browser needs usable server addresses. They may be cached; otherwise a resolver queries DNS for IPv4 or IPv6 addresses. DNS does not retrieve the page or necessarily query root servers each time. The browser uses the addresses after obtaining a valid result.
本例用 TCP 的可靠、有序字节流承载网页请求；连接出错仍可能失败。实时通话更关: This example carries requests over TCP's reliable, ordered byte stream, though connection failures remain possible. Live calls prioritize playback deadlines and may use UDP with timely loss handling, retransmission and rate control. UDP itself guarantees no low latency. HTTP/3 uses QUIC's reliable streams over UDP, not bare UDP for pages.
先看图中的简化请求：传输层添加 TCP 头，网络层添加 IP 头，再由链路层封装: In the simplified request, transport adds a TCP header, the internet layer adds IP, and the link layer wraps a frame. Ports distinguish endpoints, IP addresses enable routing, and link information serves the current hop. Real traffic may be segmented and HTTPS uses TLS. One drawn block does not mean a whole page fits in one packet.
逐跳转发：尽力送往目的地: Forward hop by hop: best effort
路由器根据目的 IP 和路由表选择下一跳，每一跳使用相应的链路封装。IP 尽力转: Routers choose the next hop using the destination IP and routing table; each hop uses its link encapsulation. IP does not guarantee delivery, order or no duplicates. The receiver processes layers up to the application. TCP adds acknowledgments and retransmission, but cannot overcome every outage. Responses also travel back through the network.
CPU 按指令工作，反复进行取指、译码和执行。: A CPU repeatedly fetches, decodes and executes instructions.
先看层级：寄存器、缓存、内存、存储，通常越往后越慢。: Registers, cache, RAM and storage are typically slower down the hierarchy.
CPU 内的控制、运算和寄存器各有分工。: Control logic, arithmetic and registers each have a role.
取指 → 译码 → 执行是概括，不等于一个时钟周期。: Fetch → Decode → Execute is a summary, not one clock cycle.
CPU 处理指令通常概括为哪三个基本阶段？: What are the three basic stages commonly used to describe instruction processing?
取指、译码、执行是基本过程的概括，具体指令还可能读写内存或写回结果；指令周期不等: Fetch, decode and execute summarize the basic process. An instruction may also access memory or write back results. An instruction cycle is not a clock cycle.
缓存是桌边那摞常用书: Cache keeps frequently used data close
缓存保留部分指令和数据的副本，命中可减少访问主内存的等待。: Cache stores copies of some instructions and data; hits reduce waits for main memory.
CPU 运算与访问主内存存在速度差，具体延迟取决于硬件。: CPU computation and RAM access differ in speed; latency depends on hardware.
为减少等待，在处理器与主内存之间设置多级缓存。: Multiple cache levels reduce waits between the processor and RAM.
能否命中缓存取决于访问模式，不是容量够大就总能命中。: Hits depend on access patterns, not just having a large cache.
CPU 与内存的速度差太大: There is a large CPU–memory speed gap
为了让程序更好写: To make programs easier to write
缓存用于缓解处理器与主内存的速度差；利用重复或相邻访问的局部性，命中时可减少等待: Cache bridges the processor–memory speed gap by exploiting repeated and nearby accesses. Hits can reduce waits, but benefits depend on hardware and the program.
常见主内存保存运行中的代码和数据，断电后不能可靠保留。: Ordinary main memory holds running code and data but does not reliably retain them without power.
程序运行时，所需代码和数据通常按需进入内存。: Programs usually bring needed code and data into RAM on demand.
常见主内存需要供电，断电后不能可靠保留数据。: Ordinary RAM needs power to retain data reliably.
要长期保存，必须落到磁盘这类非易失存储上。: Long-term retention needs nonvolatile storage such as a drive.
只存在于普通 DRAM 中、没有保存或恢复副本的修改，突然断电后应如何看待？: How should changes held only in ordinary DRAM, with no saved or recovery copy, be treated after sudden power loss?
自动写入磁盘: They are automatically written to disk
无法保证找回，应按丢失处理: Recovery is not guaranteed; treat them as lost
保留到下次开机: They remain until the next startup
普通 DRAM 断电后不能可靠保留内容，但不代表每一位瞬间清零；未保存且没有持久: Ordinary DRAM cannot reliably retain contents without power, though not every bit instantly becomes zero. Unsaved changes without persistent recovery copies are usually unrecoverable.
SSD 和机械盘通常比内存慢，但能在断电后保留已落盘的数据。: SSDs and hard drives are usually slower than RAM but retain persisted data without power.
机械盘随机访问常为毫秒级，不能把这当成 SSD 的延迟。: Hard-drive random access often takes milliseconds; this is not an SSD latency estimate.
SSD 没有机械寻道和旋转等待，随机访问通常更快。: SSDs have no mechanical seek or rotation delay and usually offer faster random access.
本章的普通应用读文件时，所需数据通常先进入内存。: For the ordinary apps here, file data usually enters RAM before use.
关于 SSD 和机械硬盘，哪个说法是对的？: Which statement about SSDs and hard drives is correct?
SSD 没有机械寻道，随机访问通常更快: SSDs avoid mechanical seeks and usually have faster random access
SSD 已落盘的数据断电就会全部清空: An SSD loses all persisted data when power is cut
机械硬盘读写一定比 SSD 快: Hard drives always read and write faster than SSDs
SSD 使用闪存，不需要磁头寻道和盘片旋转等待，随机访问通常更快；具体性能取决于: SSDs use flash rather than seeking heads and rotating platters, so random access is usually faster. Actual performance depends on device and workload; random and sequential throughput are not necessarily equal.
计算机只认得通和断，0 和 1 是它唯一的字母表。: Computers represent data using two logical states: 0 and 1.
一位只有两种状态：通电记作 1，断电记作 0。: A bit has two states, modeled as on = 1 and off = 0.
八位捆成一个字节，能表示 2 的 8 次方，共 256 种。: Eight bits make a byte: 2 to the power of 8 gives 256 combinations.
01000001 当无符号数读是 65，按 ASCII 读是 A。: 01000001 is unsigned 65, or A in ASCII.
一个字节（byte）能表示多少种不同的值？: How many distinct values can one byte represent?
取决于操作系统: It depends on the operating system
1 字节 = 8 位，每位 0 或 1，共 2^8 = 256 种组合。: One byte has 8 bits, each 0 or 1, giving 2^8 = 256 combinations.
二进制每一位的权重是 2 的幂，往左一格就翻一倍。: Binary place values are powers of two; each step left doubles the weight.
从最右边开始，各位的权重是 1、2、4、8、16……: Starting at the right, weights are 1, 2, 4, 8, 16…
往左每走一格，权重翻一倍，这就是「二进制」。: Each position left doubles the weight: base two.
按无符号整数解释，把为 1 的位权相加就是数值。: For unsigned integers, add the weights of the 1 bits.
8 + 0 + 2 + 0 = 10；选 8 是只看最高位，选 20 是把二进制: 8 + 0 + 2 + 0 = 10. Choosing 8 ignores the other set bit; 20 misreads the binary places.
固定宽度的二补码表示有符号整数，让加减法共用加法电路。: Fixed-width two's complement represents signed integers and lets addition circuits support subtraction too.
固定八位二补码：最高位 0 表示非负，1 表示负。: In eight-bit two's complement, top bit 0 means nonnegative and 1 means negative.
求负数补码：绝对值写成八位无符号数，取反加一，只留低八位。: To encode a negative, write its magnitude in eight bits, invert and add one, keeping eight bits.
-1 的八位补码加 1，丢弃最高进位后得到 0。: Adding 1 to eight-bit -1 gives 0 after discarding carry-out.
8 位补码里，-1 的二进制是？: What is -1 in eight-bit two's complement?
固定八位，先把绝对值 1 写成 0000 0001，逐位取反得 1111 111: Write magnitude 1 as 0000 0001, invert to 1111 1110, then add one: 1111 1111. Interpreted as eight-bit two's complement, that is -1.
Unicode 为字符分配码点，UTF-8 将码点编码为变长字节。: Unicode assigns code points; UTF-8 encodes them as variable-length bytes.
字符本身不是数字，得先按对照表换成编号。: Characters need a mapping to numeric codes before storage.
ASCII 只有 128 个编码位置，不包含中文。: ASCII has 128 code positions and does not include Chinese characters.
UTF-8：ASCII 字符 1 字节，常用汉字 3 字节，部分汉字 4 字节。: UTF-8 uses one byte for ASCII, three for common Chinese characters, and four for some others.
“中”这样的常用汉字，用 UTF-8 编码占几个字节？: How many UTF-8 bytes encode the common Chinese character “中”?
“中”（U+4E2D）在 UTF-8 中占 3 字节，但不是所有汉字都固定三字节: “中” (U+4E2D) occupies 3 UTF-8 bytes. Not all Chinese characters do: the extension ideograph “𠀀” (U+20000) uses 4. Text must be read with the correct encoding.
代码不是一步变成程序的: Source code needs more than one step
以常见 C 工具链为例，源码要经过编译、汇编和链接等工序。: A typical C toolchain uses compilation, assembly, linking and other steps.
起点是源码，一段人写的文本。: The starting point is source: text written by a person.
图中编译一栏合并了预处理、编译和汇编。: The compile panel combines preprocessing, compilation and assembly.
此时拿到的是目标文件，还不能直接运行。: The result is an object file, not yet a runnable program.
常见 C 工具链生成的可重定位目标文件（.o）能直接当程序运行吗？: Can a relocatable .o file from a typical C toolchain run directly as a program?
这类 .o 可含机器码、数据、符号表及重定位信息，还需链接成适合加载的程序文件；: A .o file may contain machine code, data, symbols and relocation information. It must be linked into a loadable program; it is not directly executable itself.
链接把多个目标文件和库拼成一个能跑起来的整体。: Linking combines object files and libraries into a runnable whole.
一个项目有很多源文件，各自编译成 .o。: A project has many source files, each compiled to an object file.
它们互相调用，但彼此并不知道对方在哪。: They call each other without yet knowing all final addresses.
链接器解析符号并处理重定位，部分工作可留到运行时。: The linker resolves symbols and relocations; some work may remain for runtime.
报错 undefined reference to xxx 通常是哪一步的问题？: Where does “undefined reference to xxx” usually arise?
链接时找不到符号定义: A missing symbol definition during linking
在常见 C 工具链中，编译会检查源码并生成目标文件；链接时若引用的符号找不到定义: In typical C toolchains, compilation checks source and produces objects. If linking cannot find a referenced definition, such as a function implementation or library, it commonly reports this error.
编译生成另一种代码表示，解释由执行器运行；两者可以结合。: Compilation produces another code representation; interpretation executes through an evaluator. Both can be combined.
编译可生成机器码，也可生成字节码等中间表示。: Compilers may output machine code or intermediate forms such as bytecode.
解释执行不等于逐行读源码，也可以执行字节码。: Interpretation is not necessarily line-by-line source reading; it may execute bytecode.
执行方式取决于实现；上图只是 C 工具链的示例。: Execution depends on the implementation; the diagram is only a C example.
不启用 JIT 时，CPython 通常怎样执行 .py 源码？: Without JIT, how does CPython usually execute .py source?
先编译成字节码，再由解释器执行: Compiles to bytecode, then interprets it
必须手动编译成 exe: Requires manual compilation to an exe
CPython 将源码编译成字节码后执行。字节码可缓存在 .pyc 文件中，但执: CPython compiles source to bytecode for execution. Bytecode may be cached in .pyc files, but execution does not require writing one first. A directly run main script normally does not create that cache.
静态检查在运行前读代码，把能确定的错误提前揪出来。: Static checks inspect code before execution to catch errors they can determine.
类型检查只看代码本身，不需要真的跑起来。: Type checking examines code without needing to run it.
静态类型语言通常能提前发现未声明名称或类型不匹配。: Static typing can often catch undeclared names and type mismatches early.
要等运行才知道的错误，代价通常更高。: Errors found only at runtime can be more costly.
在不允许字符串隐式转整数的静态类型语言中，哪项可直接由类型检查发现？: In a statically typed language with no implicit string-to-integer conversion, which can type checking directly catch?
把字符串赋给整型变量: Assigning a string to an integer variable
按题设，字符串赋给整型变量违反类型规则。越界或除零若取值已知，也可能在编译时发现: Under the stated rules, assigning a string to an integer violates typing. Bounds and division errors may also be detected at compile time when values are known. Input-dependent cases need runtime checks; error categories do not belong exclusively to one stage.
以 TCP 为例：逐层添加协议头，对端再逐层处理。: In this TCP example, layers add headers; the receiver processes the corresponding layers.
图中用 HTTP/1.1 请求作示例，省略 TLS 与分段。: The diagram uses HTTP/1.1, omitting TLS and segmentation.
本例传输层加 TCP 头，包含端口与序号。: Transport adds a TCP header with ports and sequence numbers.
网络层加 IP 头，写上源地址和目的地址。: The internet layer adds source and destination IP addresses.
以太网添加帧头、帧尾，承载这一跳的数据。: Ethernet adds a header and trailer for this hop.
图中的 TCP 封装示例，从应用数据往下到链路层时会怎样？: What happens as application data moves down this TCP encapsulation example?
依次添加 TCP 头、IP 头和链路封装: TCP, IP and link encapsulation are added in order
只有最底层加头: Only the bottom layer adds a header
这个简化示例依次添加 TCP 头、IP 头和以太网帧头帧尾；接收端按对应层处理。: This simplified example adds TCP, IP, then an Ethernet header and trailer; the receiver processes corresponding layers. TLS, segmentation and byte scale are omitted. Other transports do not all use TCP headers.
TCP 与 UDP 的分工: TCP and UDP serve different needs
TCP 提供可靠有序字节流；UDP 不内建重传与保序。: TCP offers a reliable ordered byte stream; UDP has no built-in retransmission or ordering.
TCP 建立连接，用序号、确认与重传提供有序字节流。: TCP uses connections, sequence numbers, acknowledgments and retransmission.
TCP 遇到丢包可能等待补齐；断网等故障仍会让传输失败。: TCP may wait for lost data; outages can still cause failure.
UDP 本身不重传、不保序，延迟并无保证；图中头部仅示例 TCP。: UDP itself neither retransmits nor orders, and guarantees no latency. The diagram shows TCP only.
实时语音希望过期数据不阻塞新数据，选择 UDP 的合理理由是？: Why might real-time voice use UDP to avoid old data blocking newer data?
UDP 保证所有数据按时到达: UDP guarantees every packet arrives on time
应用可按时效取舍丢包与重传: The app can trade off loss and retransmission by deadline
UDP 在任何网络上都比 TCP 快: UDP is faster on every network
实时媒体可在 UDP 上按播放期限选择丢弃、纠错或有限重传，而不必等待所有旧数据: Media over UDP can choose dropping, correction or limited retries by playback deadline rather than waiting for all old data. The app or upper protocol still needs congestion control; UDP promises no low latency. TCP offers reliable ordering; QUIC also supplies reliable streams over UDP.
IP 按地址尽力转发，不保证送达、顺序或不重复。: IP forwards by address without guaranteeing delivery, order or no duplicates.
IP 头里最关键的是源地址和目的地址。: Source and destination addresses are central IP header fields.
路由器按目的地址查表，决定下一跳往哪走。: Routers look up the destination to choose a next hop.
IP 不保证送达与顺序，可靠性由上层按需补充。: Higher layers add reliability when needed; IP does not guarantee it.
「IP 是尽力而为的服务」是什么意思？: What does “IP is best effort” mean?
尽力转发，但不保证送达和顺序: It tries to forward without guaranteeing delivery or order
只在局域网内有效: It only works on a local network
尽力而为是不承诺送达、顺序或不重复，并非完全不处理错误。TCP 可补充可靠传输；: Best effort means no guarantee of delivery, ordering or no duplicates, not an absence of all error handling. TCP adds reliability. UDP itself does not, but its applications or upper protocols may do so.
打开网页前先问路: Find the address before the page
DNS 查询域名信息；HTTP 定义请求与响应。: DNS looks up domain information; HTTP defines requests and responses.
域名的可用地址可能来自缓存，也可能需要 DNS 查询。: Usable addresses may be cached or require DNS queries.
DNS 的 A、AAAA 记录分别提供 IPv4、IPv6 地址。: DNS A and AAAA records provide IPv4 and IPv6 addresses.
图示为 HTTP/1.1 经 TCP；HTTP/3 使用 QUIC。: The diagram shows HTTP/1.1 over TCP; HTTP/3 uses QUIC.
访问 https://example.com 时，DNS 的作用是？: When visiting https://example.com, what does DNS do?
把域名解析成 IP 地址: Resolves the domain to IP addresses
这里 DNS 的作用是取得域名对应的 IP 地址，不是加密网页或建立 TCP 连: Here DNS obtains IP addresses, not webpage encryption or a TCP connection. HTTPS uses TLS for transport security; HTTP/3 uses QUIC over UDP, so not every web connection is TCP.
快慢差的是数量级: Latency can differ by orders of magnitude
访问寄存器、主存和存储设备的延迟可能相差多个数量级，不能用一组固定数字概括。: Register, RAM and storage latencies can differ by several orders of magnitude; no fixed numbers describe every system.
寄存器访问通常比主存访问快；具体延迟取决于硬件和操作。: Registers are usually faster than RAM; actual latency depends on hardware and operation.
SSD 与机械盘差别很大；读文件命中内存缓存时，不必访问设备。: SSDs differ from hard drives; a file-cache hit may avoid device access.
先测量瓶颈：可能在 IO、锁等待或计算，别只凭直觉优化。: Measure the bottleneck: I/O, lock waits or computation may dominate.
循环原本只做少量计算，下面哪项最可能引入明显的等待？: Which change is most likely to add substantial waiting to a loop with little computation?
每轮都同步等待未命中缓存的磁盘读取: Synchronously waiting for an uncached disk read every iteration
反复同步等待实际存储设备读取，可能远比少量计算耗时；具体影响取决于设备、缓存、访: Repeated synchronous waits for real storage reads may far outweigh a little computation. The impact depends on devices, caching, access patterns and load, not a guaranteed slowdown factor.
流水线让不同指令的处理阶段重叠；这里用四级教学模型说明。: A pipeline overlaps stages from different instructions. This example uses four teaching stages.
图中简化为取指、译码、执行、写回四级，并非所有 CPU 都是四级。: Fetch, decode, execute and write-back form this model; not every CPU has four stages.
在这个模型中，不同阶段的电路可以同时处理不同指令。: Different stage circuits can process different instructions at the same time.
四条指令错开进入；填满后且没有停顿时，这个模型每周期完成一条。: After filling, this model completes one instruction per cycle when there are no stalls.
单条指令的执行时间: The execution time of one instruction
流水线主要靠重叠提高吞吐量，不保证缩短单条指令的延迟；数据依赖、资源冲突和分支处: Overlapping stages mainly improves throughput, not necessarily single-instruction latency. Data dependencies, resource conflicts and branches can limit the benefit.
切换正在运行的线程需要保存和恢复现场，会消耗时间，并不直接推进应用任务。: Switching threads saves and restores execution state, using time without directly advancing the application task.
先看单个逻辑处理器：调度器可以把执行机会从一个线程交给另一个。: On one logical processor, a scheduler can hand execution from one thread to another.
换人之前，得把寄存器、栈指针这些现场存好。: First save state such as registers and the stack pointer.
同进程线程共享地址空间；跨地址空间切换还可能涉及页表和缓存影响。: Threads share a process address space; switching spaces may also involve page tables and caches.
线程开得越多，程序一定越快吗？: Do more threads always make a program faster?
是，线程越多越快: Yes; more threads always mean more speed
不一定，切换和竞争都有成本: No; switching and contention have costs
取决于硬盘型号: It depends on the hard-drive model
线程过多会带来频繁上下文切换和锁竞争，这些开销可能超过并行带来的收益。: Too many threads can cause frequent context switches and lock contention. Those costs may outweigh parallel gains.
并发是组织多个可独立推进的任务；并行是同时执行，两者可以同时成立。: Concurrency organizes independently progressing tasks; parallelism executes simultaneously. A system can have both.
只有一个逻辑处理器时，也能通过交替调度推进多个任务。: Even one logical processor can advance multiple tasks by scheduling them in turns.
多核可实现并行；支持 SMT 的物理核也能同时执行多个硬件线程。: Multiple cores allow parallelism; SMT can also run hardware threads on one physical core.
并发可帮助利用等待时间；并行能否提速，还要看任务可拆分程度和开销。: Concurrency can use waiting time; parallel speedups depend on how work splits and on overhead.
假设只有一个逻辑处理器且不使用 SMT，十个线程交替执行属于哪种情况？: With one logical processor and no SMT, what are ten threads running in turns an example of?
并行，因为线程多: Parallelism, because there are many threads
在题设的单逻辑处理器模型下，多个线程交替获得执行机会，属于并发而非线程间并行；不: Under the stated single-logical-processor model, alternating threads are concurrent rather than parallel with each other. Do not generalize this to every single-physical-core CPU.
